key_reasoning.reason: Four components across three subsystems: a new npm-prefix utility module (self-prefix derivation, legacy-prefix path, path comparison, user/global prefix lookup) consumed by shared utilities (processes, cli-updater, cli-bin), a new doctor health check (NpmPrefixOverrideCheck) registered in the doctor command, and both platform installers (install.sh, install.ps1) plus install README. Shared-utility involvement is already part of the L definition, so no extra bump.

No exact precedent for deriving the npm global prefix from the running package's install layout; cross-platform path rules (win32 case-insensitivity, codemie.cmd marker, POSIX lib/node_modules layout) and installers that mutate the user's npm config (npm config delete prefix --location user) with printed revert commands. Self-update targeting the wrong prefix would strand installs. Several post-review fix commits (win32 marker, fallback --prefix, DryRun truthfulness) confirm moderate risk. Existing Vitest templates covered the platform-variant tests, so no edge-case bump.

15 files changed (818 insertions): 2 new source files (npm-prefix.ts, NpmPrefixOverrideCheck.ts), 1 new test (npm-prefix.test.ts), 12 modified across install/, src/utils/, src/cli/commands/doctor/ - 11-15 file band maps to XL.

Core goal (stop the legacy per-user npm prefix override and make self-update target the running copy) was clear, but follow-up fixes to win32 install detection, fallback command text and installer dry-run output show minor gaps resolved during review.
